title: Uses of the poles table
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y6 lesson 10 (Uses of the poles table (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 10: How people use the polar regions. To understand how people use the polar regions and why they need protecting

questions.q: Name one way people use the Arctic.
questions.a: For example: oil and gas, fishing, homes and towns, tourism
questions.model: Think of resources: oil and gas. Think of food: fishing. Pick one: fishing.

questions.q: What did the 1991 agreement ban in Antarctica?
Why do scientists drill ice cores?
questions.a: To learn about past climates from the air trapped in the ice

questions.q: Core: Make a table of uses of the poles (science, resources, tourism) with one benefit and one problem for each.
questions.a: Science: learn about climate / waste from bases. Resources: fuel and food / pollution and harm to wildlife. Tourism: money and awareness / disturbs wildlife.
questions.model: Teacher shows row 1: 'Science: benefit: we learn how the climate is changing. Problem: bases make waste that must be removed.'

questions.q: Extend: Write a paragraph: should mining stay banned in Antarctica? Use the portal response box.
questions.a: For example: Yes, because mining would harm wildlife and ice, and Antarctica is kept for peace and science

questions.q: Stretch: Why is it harder to protect the Arctic than Antarctica?
questions.a: The Arctic belongs to several countries with people and industries; Antarctica is governed by one shared treaty

questions.q: Big question: should anyone be allowed to dig for oil in Antarctica?
questions.a: Reasoned view, for example: no, because it would harm a fragile place kept for peace and science
